newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican confirms Pope's surgery for Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Vatican confirms Pope's surgery for Tuesday.

text.p: The Vatican confirmed on Monday that Pope John Paul would have an operation to remove his appendix on Tuesday at Rome's Gemelli hospital.

Chief spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls said the 76-year-old Pope, who was admitted to the hospital on Sunday night, had routine examinations early on Monday before celebrating mass in the special suite he occupies on the 10th floor of the Gemelli.
"I confirm that tomorrow morning, Tuesday October 8, the Holy Father John Paul II will undergo the planned operation... at the Agostino Gemelli Hospital," Navarro-Valls said in his written statement.
The head of the team which will carry out the surgery, Professor Francesco Crucitti, earlier said the Pope had spent a restful night at the hospital.
Giuseppe Pallanch, spokesman for the Gemelli, told reporters the first medical bulletin on the Pope's condition would be issued after 0900 GMT on Tuesday, once the operation was over.
The Vatican announced the planned surgery last month in a statement which said recurrent inflammation of the appendix was the cause of three "intestinal fevers" the Pope has suffered since Christmas.
